*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: c:\Users\linus\git\3\context-engine\.agents\instructions\orchestration\core-cycle.instructions.md
+---
+description: "Use when turning a request into production work or reporting validated results. Covers the closed-loop production cycle: request -> spec -> tickets -> tests -> implementation -> validated response -> next iteration."
+applyTo: "**/*.md,**/*.toml"
+---
+
+## Core Cycle
+
+Use this named production cycle to make work traceable from a request through
+the user's next judgment. It complements [phase separation](phase-separation.instructions.md), which owns discovery versus implementation boundaries, and [loop closure](loop-closure.instructions.md), which owns Review -> Interview -> Commit -> Handoff.
+
+| Stage | Enter when | Exit when | Handoff artifact |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1. Request | A user ask or raw transcript exists. | The intended outcome and open questions are captured. | The request or refined dossier. |
+| 2. Spec | The work needs a durable goal and definition of success. | The spec defines the goal, owned acceptance criteria, and required traceability. | A reviewed spec and criterion references. |
+| 3. Tickets | The spec is ready to plan implementation. | Tickets reference the spec and define executable slices. | Ticket plan, dependencies, and spec references. |
+| 4. Tests | Tickets expose acceptance criteria to measure. | Validation evidence is recorded, or the criterion is explicitly documented without executable validation. | Test/validation records linked to the ticket, spec, and applicable criteria. |

+# Production Workflow Cycle
+
+## Purpose
+
+Define the complete production workflow as a closed cycle: Request -> Spec ->
+Tickets -> Tests -> Implementation -> Validated response -> Next iteration.
+Each stage is a component that owns only its outward-facing obligations. The
+following records are deliberately shaped to migrate mechanically into the
+Waypoint 2 component-oriented artifact model.
+
+## Target-model Encoding
+
+`spec_id` in each record is this spec's id after creation. `context`,
+`related_spec_ids`, `related_evidence_ids`, and `code_refs` are optional
+component fields and are omitted when empty. Criteria without `validated_by`
+are complete documented requirements, not failed validation.
+
+### Evidence References
+
+| id | spec_id | target_kind | target_ref | relation | locator |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| ev-core-cycle | `<this-spec-id>` | instruction | `.agents/instructions/orchestration/core-cycle.instructions.md` | defines | `Core Cycle; Contract Rules` |

+- `spec_id`: `<this-spec-id>`
+- `title`: `Spec`
+- `purpose`: Define the durable goal, provider-owned acceptance criteria, and traceability before implementation planning.

+- `spec_id`: `<this-spec-id>`
+- `title`: `Tickets`

+### Component: tests

+- `spec_id`: `<this-spec-id>`

+- `purpose`: Record the user's judgment and either close the loop or convert follow-up into the next request.

+
+| id | owner_component_id | statement | validated_by |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| next-iteration-judgment | `workflow-cycle.next-iteration` | The user's satisfaction or follow-up judgment is recorded. | [`ev-core-cycle`] |
+| next-iteration-transition | `workflow-cycle.next-iteration` | A follow-up judgment becomes the next Request input; a satisfied judgment closes the cycle. | [`ev-core-cycle`, `ev-loop-closure`] |

+## Directed Contract Edges
+
+Each downstream consumer owns its dependency edge and references provider-owned
+criteria without copying them. The final edge intentionally closes the cycle.

turns.content:
**Research Question / Anchor**

Why did two `/spec` dispatches create flat, boilerplate-heavy roots? Anchor: [Production Workflow Cycle](.spec/specs/90e4fb79-2c60-42a6-ab10-91d243693150/spec.toml) and [Spec Agent](.agents/agents/spec.agent.md).

**Root Cause: Granularity**

1. **Actively caused:** [ROADMAP.v5](transcripts/22-08-2026_spec-system-workflow-cycle/ROADMAP.v5.md#L57) says “author spec entities ... for each cycle component” while also saying to use the old tooling “as dogmatically as the model ... allows.” The target model’s root-scoped component records were therefore encoded inside one old-format spec root.
2. **Actively enabled:** [core-cycle instructions](.agents/instructions/orchestration/core-cycle.instructions.md#L24) say, “Each component owns its outward-facing acceptance criteria,” but provide no requirement that the component own a separate spec entity.
3. **Failed to prevent:** [spec-system instructions](.agents/instructions/spec/spec-system.instructions.md#L61) say, “Prefer a parent spec only when the new slice is clearly a child of an existing broader contract.” This makes creating a new parent followed by children non-obvious and optional.
4. **Failed to prevent:** [spec prompt](.agents/prompts/spec.prompt.md#L16) says only to identify “the best component and parent”; [Spec Agent](.agents/agents/spec.agent.md#L34) says “create a draft spec” singular. Neither requires a component map, a root, or child specs.
5. **Verified absence:** no spec-governing instruction mandates or mentions one-spec-per-component. The only spec instruction is [spec-system instructions](.agents/instructions/spec/spec-system.instructions.md).

**Root Cause: Boilerplate / Underspecification**

1. **Active source:** the same roadmap requires the target component/criterion/evidence/edge model; its artifact shape, not a checked-in spec template, produced the repeated records and tables. No checked-in guidance contains the exact headings `Target-model Encoding` or `Components And Provider-Owned Criteria`.
2. **Failed quality gate:** [spec-system instructions](.agents/instructions/spec/spec-system.instructions.md#L66) mandates five generic sections, including governing rules and readiness positions, but has no minimum substantive-content test for a component purpose, behavior, boundary, inputs/outputs, or failure modes.
3. **Defect evidence:** the 169-line [body](.spec/specs/90e4fb79-2c60-42a6-ab10-91d243693150/body.md#L11) is roughly 85% IDs, repeated metadata, tables, edges, observations, and matrices. The `request` purpose is verbatim: “Capture the requested outcome and any open questions that must be resolved before durable planning.” [body](.spec/specs/90e4fb79-2c60-42a6-ab10-91d243693150/body.md#L29)
4. **Prompt defect:** [spec prompt](.agents/prompts/spec.prompt.md#L12) references `../../agents/skills/SPEC_TOOL.md`, which does not exist, so its promised store-layout guidance was unavailable.

**Authority Map**

Canonical owner today: [spec-system instructions](.agents/instructions/spec/spec-system.instructions.md), despite [core-cycle instructions](.agents/instructions/orchestration/core-cycle.instructions.md#L28) claiming the prompt owns “spec authoring.” The new granularity rule should live in `spec-system.instructions.md`; the prompt and agent should operationalize it without redefining it.

**Competing-Rule Check**

+# Component-Oriented Specification System
+
+## Motivation
+
+Define a code-first, component-owned specification model whose durable manifest
+data, markdown navigation, generated index, CLI output, and health enforcement
+can be reviewed as one traceable contract.
+
+## Reading Order
+
+1. [.agents/instructions/spec/spec-system.instructions.md](.agents/instructions/spec/spec-system.instructions.md) - canonical authoring and relationship-traceability rules.
+2. [90e4fb79 Production Workflow Cycle](.spec/specs/90e4fb79-2c60-42a6-ab10-91d243693150/body.md) - governing request-to-spec-to-ticket workflow neighbor.
+3. [a608f774 Specification Root Contract](.spec/specs/a608f774-9f50-4de1-90e2-ffeefb0198b1/body.md) - root namespace and surviving manifest fields.
+4. [fdb7645d Component Artifact Contract](.spec/specs/fdb7645d-eac5-4b82-88eb-94cb22f1b0b2/body.md) - code-facing component participant and required location metadata.
+5. [aebcbab4 Criterion Artifact Contract](.spec/specs/aebcbab4-2827-4ea1-8244-0a2e6277b571/body.md) - provider-owned acceptance obligations.
+6. [7498bed7 Evidence Reference Contract](.spec/specs/7498bed7-ac74-4484-b50e-8a9cf96d8431/body.md) - external evidence identity and location.
+7. [ad0685f5 Directed Contract Edge](.spec/specs/ad0685f5-cb35-4c61-b1dc-f69232521e25/body.md) - persisted consumer-to-provider criterion edges.
+8. [83c0b9c4 Validation Observation Contract](.spec/specs/83c0b9c4-1617-4751-af23-57811060f0fb/body.md) - optional criterion evidence outcomes.
+9. [55d8f2eb Specification Store Contract](.spec/specs/55d8f2eb-70f1-4b90-8c8f-e50d5e311d48/body.md) - manifest persistence, hierarchy, and catalog rendering.
+10. [b4475214 Specification Health Check](.spec/specs/b4475214-e14e-4926-b853-b2553444e36f/body.md) - structural, parity, hierarchy, and example checks.
+11. [f482eb83 Ticket Store Integration](.spec/specs/f482eb83-5b47-4ea3-8d5b-b7baa0531333/body.md) - governed-ticket prerequisite.
+12. [73817390 Document Store Evidence Integration](.spec/specs/73817390-7e6a-427a-a644-626718d9f25d/body.md) - stable document targets.
+13. [89360ad7 Validation Store Evidence Integration](.spec/specs/89360ad7-d638-49e7-85ba-21839fa99851/body.md) - validation evidence and hook enforcement.
+
+## Component Relationship Map
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+    Root[Specification Root] -->|root-artifact-namespace| Store[Specification Store]
+    Root -->|ticket-governing-spec| Ticket[Ticket Store]
+    Component[Component Artifact] -->|root-artifact-namespace| Root
+    Criterion[Criterion Artifact] -->|component-criterion-ownership| Component
+    Criterion -->|root-artifact-namespace| Root
+    Evidence[Evidence Reference] -->|root-artifact-namespace| Root
+    Evidence -->|document-stable-target, document-resolution-result| Document[Document Store]
+    Edge[Directed Contract Edge] -->|component-root-membership| Component
+    Edge -->|criterion-single-owner, criterion-root-unique| Criterion
+    Edge -->|stored typed edges| Store
+    Observation[Validation Observation] -->|criterion-required-fields| Criterion
+    Observation -->|evidence-required-fields| Evidence
+    Observation -->|validation-observation-source| Validation[Validation Store]
+    Health[Health Check] -->|store-persists-artifacts, parent integrity| Store
+    Health -->|toml-body link parity, examples| Edge
+    Validation -->|hook enforcement| Health
+    Store -->|parent link list and graph verification| Component
+```
+
+## Shared Invariants
+
+- A provider exclusively owns criteria; a consumer stores only its directed edge
+  to provider criterion ids and never copies provider statements.
+- Every code-facing child has a manifest `code_refs` location and a concrete
+  naming convention; every parent body lists and graphs its direct children.
+- The future structured links in `spec.toml` and the clickable links in `body.md`
+  must represent the same edge set. This is a draft requirement: current health
+  checks do not parse body links or persist component edges.
+- An unvalidated criterion remains structurally complete. Health reports shape,
+  reference, hierarchy, and authored-document drift rather than fulfillment.
+
+## Examples
+
+A specification root with component `spec-api` declares a `Health Check`
+component. Its manifest stores the component's `code_refs`, its body links the
+Specification Store provider, and its `health-link-parity` criterion is consumed
+by a Validation Store hook edge. The catalog renderer then verifies that this
+root lists the Health Check child and includes the matching graph node and edge.
+
+## Scope
+
+This draft root owns only the cross-component navigation and invariants. The
+eleven existing children own behavior, failure cases, provider criteria, and
+evidence; no implementation ticket is linked pending user review.

+# Specification Query And Link Resolution CLI
+
+## Target Code Location
+

+
+Use `spec dump <id>` for the complete projection and `spec links <id>` for resolved links. This child owns `query-spec-dump` and `query-resolved-links`.

+

+

+
+`spec dump <id> --json` returns id, timestamps, fields, code refs, components, criteria, evidence, observations, edges, sections, and body. `spec links <id> --json` returns link kind, source field, target, resolution result, and failure detail.

+- `query-spec-dump`: emit all persisted data for an unambiguous spec id, including structured extras and `code_refs`.
+- `query-resolved-links`: enumerate and resolve every TOML-backed spec, code, ticket, document, and component-edge link; do not infer body-only links as structured data.

-
-# Production Workflow Cycle
-
-## Motivation
-
-This root defines the traceable path from a user request to that user's next
-judgment. It keeps planning, validation, execution, and follow-up connected
-without making a ticket or an implementation agent redefine the requirement.
-
-## Dependent Expectation
-
-If this specification is implemented, dependents can rely on every production
-unit progressing through Request -> Spec -> Tickets -> Tests -> Implementation
--> Validated response -> Next iteration, with a durable artifact at each handoff.
-
-## Shared Invariants
-
-- Each child owns its outward-facing acceptance criteria; a consumer names the
-  upstream criteria it requires without copying them.
-- A draft cycle contract is documentation, not a claim that an implementation or
-  executable guard exists. These specs remain draft pending user review.

Session: `2ea0b071-20c3-42c0-bfeb-463aec109daa`; worktree: main checkout on `main`.

**Prefix Registry Design**

- **Storage:** add committed root metadata at `.spec/criterion-prefixes.toml`, owned by the `.spec` index root, mapping stable component IDs to prefixes.
- **Collision scope:** the entire `SpecStore` rooted at that `.spec`, across every registered scan root, not merely one parent/child hierarchy. Existing `SpecStore` scans indexed manifests globally; `component` is only a per-manifest string, so derivation cannot detect cross-root conflicts reliably.
- **Health rule:** every component artifact resolves to exactly one registry entry; component IDs and prefixes are each unique; every criterion ID must equal `<registered-prefix>-<behavior>`; unregistered, mismatched, duplicate, or orphaned entries are findings.
- **Migration:** populate the registry, rename criteria to registered prefixes, and report legacy forms. Do not infer registry entries or semantic typed links from legacy values.

**Ticket-Gate Evidence Map**

`ValidationExecution` already supplies `Passed | Failed | Blocked` and `ValidationLinks.ticket_ids`; ticket schemas already provide `in-review`, `on-hold`, and `done`. The current release path persists flat validation fields, so it supports durable ticket metadata but has no typed gate record.

Put a typed `ValidationGateRecord` in the ticket manifest, separate from the execution: gate/criterion identity, selected execution ID, outcome, and timestamps. Recommended map: `passed` satisfies the gate; `failed` and `blocked` leave it unsatisfied. None auto-transition ticket lifecycle state; a satisfied gate authorizes the normal manual transition, preserving the existing review requirement.

**Markdown Parser Choice**

Use `markdown = "1"` with `markdown::to_mdast(..., &ParseOptions::gfm())`.

It is the existing backend parser in [workflow-tools/doc/crates/doc-viewer/Cargo.toml](workflow-tools/doc/crates/doc-viewer/Cargo.toml) and supports the mdast traversal needed for links and semantic sections. `pulldown-cmark` is currently frontend-only, so it should not be borrowed for spec health.

**Spec Contradictions To Revise**

| Short-id | Section/current claim | Required update |
|---|---|---|
| `fdb7645d` | Naming/boundaries requires a documented naming section | Require a registered component ID and registry-owned unique prefix; the section documents usage, not authority. |
| `aebcbab4` | IDs are unique “per root”; owner-prefix convention is documented locally | Replace with system-wide registry-derived IDs; retain local duplicate detection only as a subsidiary integrity check. |
| `b4475214` | Health validates local ownership/uniqueness but omits registry and detect-only migration | Add registry integrity findings and explicit legacy detect-and-report findings; health must not fall back semantically. |
| `89360ad7` | Pre-commit/git hook runs health and fails on any finding | Replace with `PostToolUse` after relevant `.spec/specs/` writes, once per repo root; block only findings not in the versioned `(spec_id, issue)` allowlist. |
| `73817390` | Resolution returns identity/location or generic resolvable failure | Specify `Resolved { record }`, `Missing { id }`, and `Unsupported { target }`; neither non-resolved state establishes success. |
| `55d8f2eb` | Renderer may emit parent navigation and fail graph/body mismatch | Parent navigation remains handwritten and verification-only; retain semantic parity checks without generated overwrite behavior. |

**Remaining Questions**

1. **Gate lifecycle policy:** should a gate outcome auto-transition its governed ticket?
   Choices: no auto-transition; `passed -> done`; `failed -> in-implementation`; `blocked -> on-hold`.
   Recommended: no auto-transition; record the gate and preserve the normal lifecycle transition.

2. **Repeated execution authority:** how does a rerun replace prior gate evidence?
   Choices: latest execution wins; first passing execution remains sufficient; ticket gate explicitly selects an execution.
   Recommended: the gate record explicitly selects the authoritative execution, updated on rerun; full history remains in test-api.

Current `spec health --all` baseline is exactly the three allowlisted `9f0b9e30` findings.

The remaining design reduces to two evidence-gate rules. The prefix registry has a concrete home at `.spec/criterion-prefixes.toml`, scoped to the whole store; the parser can use the existing backend `markdown` crate. questions.question: May one validation run supply the pass/fail result for the same requirement on more than one ticket?
questions.message: In this model, a **criterion** is one named requirement, and **evidence** is the recorded result of a test run. A ticket’s acceptance check reads the newest test result for its criterion; it does not automatically change the ticket’s lifecycle state. Example: two worktree-ctl tickets could both require `worktree-gitlink-containment`; a newer test run that passes or fails that criterion would currently be seen by both tickets. [f482eb83 Ticket Store Integration](.spec/specs/f482eb83-5b47-4ea3-8d5b-b7baa0531333/body.md) needs to record whether that sharing is intentional.

options.label: Allow shared results (recommended)
options.description: Tickets using the same criterion read the same newest result. This avoids duplicate test runs, but a later failure makes that requirement unsatisfied for every ticket that depends on it.

options.label: Require ticket-specific results
options.description: A test run must identify one ticket as well as the criterion. This isolates ticket readiness, but duplicates executions when tickets share the same requirement.

options.label: Allow a ticket-specific override
options.description: Use a shared result by default, but prefer a ticket-tagged run when one exists. This supports exceptions but adds precedence rules and more health cases.

questions.question: When one ticket names several acceptance criteria, what must be true before its evidence checks are satisfied?
questions.message: A ticket may have more than one named requirement. Example: a ticket that adds the worktree Git adapter could require both `worktree-git-operations-exist` and `worktree-gitlink-containment`; each has its own newest test result. This choice only decides the evidence check; normal review still controls any ticket state transition. [f482eb83 Ticket Store Integration](.spec/specs/f482eb83-5b47-4ea3-8d5b-b7baa0531333/body.md) needs one aggregation rule.

options.label: All criteria must pass (recommended)
options.description: Every named requirement needs a newest `passed` result. A missing, failed, or blocked result leaves the evidence check unsatisfied.

options.label: Any criterion may pass
options.description: One passing requirement is enough; simpler, but lets a ticket appear ready while other named requirements still fail.

options.label: Per-ticket expression
options.description: Each ticket stores AND/OR logic. Flexible, but introduces a policy language before there is evidence it is needed.
